command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged input against its pinned sha256 =="
printf '%s  %s\n' 683eb19310c40bf1396e4718f45afa2ce86755717c0990f47a171f535d248ea1 \
  ensembl116_cdna.fa.gz > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

echo "== salmon index: Ensembl 116 human transcriptome =="
# --ramLimit is salmon's own default (8 GiB); stated explicitly so the box's memory
# request and the tool's budget are visibly the same number rather than coincidence.
salmon index -t ensembl116_cdna.fa.gz -i sidx -p 8 --ramLimit 8 2>&1 | tee index.log

# ---- smoke check on the index itself ----
# Splitting index from quant is what makes this worth checking here: a bad index
# fails now, before 1.6 GiB crosses S3 twice. The reference count is exact — it is a
# property of the pinned transcriptome, not of anything salmon chooses.
REFS=$(awk '/^indexed .* references/ {print $2; exit}' index.log)
FILES=$(ls sidx | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
BYTES=$(du -sk sidx | cut -f1)

{
  echo "indexed_references $REFS    want exactly 453553"
  echo "index_files        $FILES   want >= 8            (observed 9)"
  echo "index_kib          $BYTES   want 1000000..2500000 (observed ~1.6 GiB)"
} > smoke-check-index.txt
cat smoke-check-index.txt

test "$REFS"  -eq 453553
test "$FILES" -ge 8
test "$BYTES" -ge 1000000
test "$BYTES" -le 2500000
test -s sidx/info.json
test -s sidx/index.ssi
test -s sidx/index.ctab
ls -la sidx

# Ship the index as ONE tar object, not as an S3 prefix. spawn does support directory
# staging (a Manifest source ending in "/" gets `aws s3 cp --recursive`), but on the
# container path an output's parent dir is never mkdir-ed before `docker run`, so
# dockerd creates it as root and the container cannot write into it. A single file
# under flat /tmp sidesteps that. See README.
tar -cf salmon-index.tar sidx
rm -rf sidx                     # free 1.6 GiB before stage-out; the tar is the artifact
test -s salmon-index.tar
echo "== index tar bytes: $(wc -c < salmon-index.tar) =="
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
